golf-handicap-calculator.assumptionNote: Uses the World Handicap System (WHS) method: score differentials from your last rounds, adjusted by the course and slope ratings of each round. Official handicaps require membership in a golf association; this is a close estimate for casual play.
benefits: Track improvement over time. A falling index is proof your practice is working.
Play fairly against golfers of any level: handicaps level the match.
Know which of your recent rounds count toward the index.
Get a number comparable to official WHS handicaps.

faqs.a: At least 3 to compute anything, and 20 for a full index. This calculator accepts 3 to 20 scores and follows the WHS table for how many of your best differentials count.
faqs.q: How many scores do I need?

faqs.a: If everyone has an index, you usually get one stroke per round equal to your index, applied on the hardest holes. Course Handicap = Handicap Index x Slope / 113 + (Course Rating - Par).
faqs.q: How do I use my index in a match?

faqs.a: Your course handicap. Take your handicap index, multiply by the slope rating, and divide by 113. A higher slope means you get more strokes.
faqs.q: What is the difference between handicap index and course handicap?

faqs.a: Roughly yes. A lower index means a better golfer. Scratch golfers are near 0. Bogey golfers sit around 18 to 22. Beginners often start at 30 or higher.
faqs.q: Is a lower handicap always better?

faqs.a: Enter each round as gross adjusted score, separated by commas, spaces, or line breaks. Example: 92, 88, 95, 90, 87. Up to 20 scores - newest rounds are the most meaningful.
faqs.q: How do I enter my scores?

faqs.a: Most scorecards print the Course Rating (like 71.5) and Slope Rating (like 128) for each tee. Check your club's website too. If you cannot find them, use par for rating and 113 for slope as a rough stand-in.
faqs.q: Where do I find course and slope ratings?

golf-handicap-calculator.formula:
Step 1: Score Differential = (Adjusted Gross Score - Course Rating) x 113 / Slope Rating
Step 2: Sort differentials, take your best N of the last 20 rounds (WHS table: 3 rounds -> 1, 6 -> 2, 9 -> 3, 12 -> 4, 15 -> 6, 17 -> 7, 19 -> 9, 20 -> 8).
Step 3: Handicap Index = average of those differentials, minus an adjustment for fewer than 6 rounds (3 rounds: -2, 4 rounds: -1, 6 rounds: -1), rounded to one decimal.

No 0.96 bonus factor under the 2020 World Handicap System - it is a straight average of your best 8 of 20.
howTo: Enter the Course Rating and Slope Rating from your scorecard (for example 71.5 and 128).
Type 3 to 20 of your recent gross scores, separated by commas or line breaks.
Your handicap index appears instantly, along with which differentials counted.
For a course handicap, use: Index x Slope / 113. Try different tees to see the effect.
keyFacts: The World Handicap System (WHS) unified handicap rules worldwide in 2020.
Handicap Index = the average of your best 8 of the last 20 score differentials.
Score Differential = (score - course rating) x 113 / slope rating.
A differential measures how you played relative to that course's difficulty.
With fewer than 20 rounds, the WHS counts fewer best scores: 3 rounds -> 1, 6 -> 2, 9 -> 3, 12 -> 4, 15 -> 6, 17 -> 7, 19 -> 9.
An adjustment is subtracted with very few rounds: -2 for 3 rounds, -1 for 4 or 6 rounds.
A lower index means a better player. Scratch golfers are near 0, beginners often above 30.
Course Handicap = Index x Slope / 113, which tells you how many strokes you get on that course.
